summary: Defines extensions to BGP Link State (BGP-LS) for advertising application-specific link attributes as part of topology information. Link-state routing protocols had already been extended to carry such attributes for applications like Segment Routing. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Different apps may care about different things on the same road, like speed or safety. This lets the shared map record those per-app facts and share them.

questions: how does bgp-ls advertise application-specific link attributes
what are application specific link attributes
what is the bgp-ls asla tlv
how does bgp-ls handle is-is application-specific srlg
subtitle: How BGP-LS tells a controller which link attributes apply to which applications, such as RSVP-TE or Segment Routing.

tldr.problem: IS-IS and OSPF were extended to say which applications (such as Segment Routing or Loop-Free Alternates) a link attribute is meant for, but BGP-LS, which hands topology to controllers, had no way to carry that.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines the Application-Specific Link Attributes (ASLA) TLV, type 1122, which holds link attributes as sub-TLVs together with bit masks naming the applications, and sets rules for translating the IGP encodings into it.
tldr.outcome: A controller can now learn per-application link attributes from BGP-LS. Consumers that do not support it keep using the older top-level TLVs for existing applications but cannot see the new application-specific data.

today: RFC 9294 is a Proposed Standard from August 2022. It has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Why Application-Specific Attributes Are Needed
sections.content:
BGP-LS carries link-state topology information from IS-IS, OSPFv2 and OSPFv3 to an application such as a controller or Path Computation Engine (PCE), using BGP. With topology from across IGP domains, the controller can compute paths for uses like end-to-end traffic engineering.

The link attributes in that topology were first defined for MPLS TE (RSVP-TE or GMPLS). Newer applications such as Segment Routing (SR) Policy and Loop-Free Alternates (LFA) also use link attributes. RFC 8919 (IS-IS) and RFC 8920 (OSPF) let an IGP say which application an attribute is for. This document adds the matching BGP-LS extension.

Attributes are carried either as top-level TLVs of the BGP-LS Attribute, or as sub-TLVs of the new top-level ASLA TLV.
sections.eli5: Roads can have different rules for buses, bikes and trucks. The map used to have only one set of rules per road. Now it can keep a separate set for each kind of traveler.

sections.title: The ASLA TLV
sections.content:
The Application-Specific Link Attributes (ASLA) TLV is an optional top-level BGP-LS Attribute TLV for Link NLRIs. It acts as a container for existing and future link attributes that need application-specific definition. Its type is 1122 and its length is variable.

After Type and Length come a 1-octet SABM Length, a 1-octet UDABM Length and a 2-octet Reserved field, which MUST be zero on transmission and ignored on reception. Then follow the Standard Application Identifier Bit Mask and the User-Defined Application Identifier Bit Mask, each 0, 4 or 8 octets as its length field says, and finally the link attribute sub-TLVs. Each bit in a mask stands for one application, with semantics as in RFC 8920.

The ASLA TLV can only be added to the BGP-LS Attribute of the Link NLRI of the node that originates the underlying IGP link attribute TLVs.
sections.eli5: Think of a labeled folder. The label says which apps the papers inside are for, and the papers are the link facts.

sections.title: Which Attributes Are Application-Specific
sections.content:
Several existing BGP-LS link TLVs can have application-specific meaning in the IGPs. The RFC lists them in a table: administrative group (1088), TE Default Metric (1092), Shared Risk Link Group (1096), the unidirectional delay, delay variation, loss and bandwidth TLVs (1114 to 1120) and Extended Administrative Group (1173).

All of these are REQUIRED to be advertised as top-level TLVs when they carry attributes specific to RSVP-TE. Attributes advertised as application-specific in the IGP are REQUIRED to be encoded within an ASLA TLV. Link attributes without application-specific semantics MUST NOT go inside the ASLA TLV.

If the same attribute appears both inside an ASLA TLV and as a top-level TLV, the ASLA value takes precedence for the applications named in the ASLA TLV.
sections.eli5: Some facts, like how fast a road is, can differ per traveler. Those go in the per-traveler folder. If a fact is in both places, the folder wins.

sections.title: Translating IGP Advertisements into BGP-LS
sections.content:
The BGP-LS originator learns which applications an attribute applies to from the IGP LSAs or LSPs it is reading. Attributes learned from an IGP node that does not use ASLA encodings continue to use the top-level TLVs.

OSPF's encoding is close to BGP-LS's, but IS-IS differs: it has an L-flag, and it splits information across two encodings, the ASLA sub-TLV and the Application-Specific SRLG TLV. The originator follows these rules:

  • Attributes from an OSPF ASLA sub-TLV, or an IS-IS ASLA sub-TLV or Application-Specific SRLG TLV, MUST go into the BGP-LS ASLA TLV as sub-TLVs, with two exceptions below.
  • If the IS-IS ASLA sub-TLV has the RSVP-TE bit set, the attributes use the top-level BGP-LS TLVs, and SRLG values use top-level TLV 1096.
  • SRLGs and other attributes from the two IS-IS encodings MUST be collated per application when the stated criteria hold. Applications with identical results MAY share one ASLA TLV.
  • Zero-length bit mask advertisements are carried into a zero-length-mask ASLA TLV, independent of collation.
  • Maximum Link Bandwidth MUST be encoded only in top-level TLV 1089. Maximum Reservable Link Bandwidth and Unreserved Bandwidth MUST be encoded only in top-level TLVs 1090 and 1091.
sections.eli5: The person copying the map from one language to another has a rulebook. It says which facts go in which folder and when to merge folders that say the same thing.

sections.title: Worked IS-IS Illustration
sections.content:
The RFC walks through one link with three IS-IS advertisements: (a) an ASLA sub-TLV with the S, F and X bits set, (b) an Application-Specific SRLG TLV with zero-length bit masks, and (c) an SRLG TLV with the X bit set.

After the rules apply, the final set is: an ASLA for S carrying attributes (a) and SRLGs (b); the same for F; an ASLA for X carrying (a); a zero-length-mask ASLA with SRLGs (b); and an ASLA for X with SRLGs (c). An implementation may further consolidate S and F into one ASLA TLV. Further optimization is outside the scope of the document.
sections.eli5: Some folders get merged and some stay apart. The example shows exactly which ones, so everyone ends up with the same map.

sections.title: Deployment and Compatibility
sections.content:
BGP-LS takes its data from the IGPs, so deployment aspects are covered in RFC 8919 and RFC 8920. The backward-compatibility procedures there, together with this document's, keep existing implementations of RFC 7752, RFC 8571 and RFC 9104 working for RSVP-TE, SR Policy and LFA.

It is recommended that only nodes supporting this specification originate BGP-LS information where application-specific link attributes are in use. Consumers that do not support it can keep using the top-level TLVs for existing applications, but cannot support application-specific attributes or newer applications encoded only in the ASLA TLV.
sections.eli5: Old map readers still understand the old folder. They just cannot read the new per-traveler folders.

sections.title: Security and Manageability
sections.content:
Security considerations for BGP-LS are in RFC 7752, especially those about traffic engineering topology information. The IGP instances that originate the underlying TLVs are assumed to provide the security required by RFC 8919 and RFC 8920.

Tampering could affect applications that use this information, including traffic engineering path computation. Because the advertisements limit scope to specific applications, the impact is similarly limited. The RFC finds no significant additional risk beyond existing link attribute information. It adds no new configuration or monitoring aspects, and IANA assigned code point 1122 for the ASLA TLV.
sections.eli5: Someone who scribbles on the map could send traffic the wrong way. Since each folder is for one kind of traveler, the damage stays small.
